section_summary: This section continues an FBI investigation of suspected Japanese espionage networks in Brazil, especially the contacts, employment, finances, correspondence, surveillance, and repatriation of Japanese residents and their Brazilian associates in Rio de Janeiro. It also discusses an anonymous allegation concerning the Black Dragon Society, possible coded correspondence, Japanese contacts in Argentina and Chile, and the South American Cotton Company’s activities in Santiago. The section then begins a January 1944 FBI submission to the State Department concerning the JAPSA case and the liquidation, personnel, finances, and suspected intelligence role of the Southern Cotton Company in Peru.

subfiles.title: Continuation of FBI investigative memorandum on Japanese contacts in Brazil and Chile
subfiles.about: Continued reporting on suspected Japanese intelligence contacts, commercial covers, correspondence, surveillance, and repatriation in Rio de Janeiro, with related information from Argentina and Chile.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum profiles Alberto Goes Telles, Ryokichi Nagai, Kanji Shirato, Tsuneo Noma, Suetaka Hayao, Ary Figueira, and numerous Japanese, Brazilian, and European associates, recording their employment, finances, addresses, contacts, and observed movements. It examines a letter to Nagai for possible coded references and an anonymous allegation that Noma and others belonged to a Black Dragon intelligence organization, while repeatedly noting when surveillance produced no derogatory evidence. Particular attention is given to Japanese repatriates departing aboard the SS Gripsholm, Hayao’s work through the Spanish Embassy, and merchants with views of Rio harbor. The closing pages reproduce intelligence on Kaname Nakayama and the South American Cotton Company’s personnel, financing, mapping, aerial-photography, and mineral-survey activities in Chile.

subfiles.title: Letter transmitting additional JAPSA case intelligence from Peru
subfiles.from: J. Edgar Hoover, Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle Jr., Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Hoover transmits an attached memorandum concerning the Southern Cotton Company and related Japanese espionage activity in Lima.
subfiles.summary: Hoover recalls that the JAPSA case concerned Japanese espionage agents operating through commercial firms across Latin America, principally the Southern Cotton Company. He forwards current information on the company’s operations in Lima and notes that accused commercial spy Akira Uesugi had been deported from Peru and repatriated aboard the SS Gripsholm. The same intelligence had been supplied to U.S. military, naval, and diplomatic representatives in Peru, Brazil, Chile, Bolivia, and Argentina.

subfiles.title: JAPSA case memorandum on the Southern Cotton Company in Peru
subfiles.about: The memorandum describes Peru’s seizure and liquidation of the Southern Cotton Company, its Japanese directors and employees, and its financial and cotton-export transactions.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum outlines Peruvian wartime legislation freezing and expropriating Axis property and explains that the Southern Cotton Company, a Mitsui and Toyo Menka Kaisha organization, ceased business after December 1941. It identifies the firm’s owners, directors, employees, salaries, deportations, and the transfer of Tatsuo Daiko’s authority to Japanese-community leader Nakataro Aray. It also inventories cotton assets and unpaid exports to Japan, noting a wartime shift from dollar to yen invoicing. The surviving pages end amid an examination of large transfers involving the Yokohama Specie Bank and Banco Italiano.
